blocking_requirements.statement: DSEx is installable as a clean Elixir package and its documented public API works outside the source checkout.
DSEx docs and Livebooks are executable product evidence, including real-provider proof cells for provider-relevant features.
DSEx implements DSPy-shaped core semantics for signatures, Predict, ChainOfThought, typed adapters, ReAct tool traces, streaming, save/load redaction, and cache behavior.
DSEx matches Python DSPy on live matched-model benchmark tasks with current prompt contracts, complete instrumentation, runtime-shape evidence, and consistent execution settings.
DSEx optimizer behavior has direct or intentionally-deviating evidence against DSPy for the optimizer surfaces it claims.

DSEx GEPA research claims are supported only by fresh GEPA paper-family replication artifacts that compare baseline, DSPy GEPA, DSEx GEPA, and MIPROv2 with cost, budget, seed, and split-gap metadata; SIMBA may be reported as extra comparator evidence when present.
DSEx RAG, tool, ReAct, agent, CodeAct, ProgramOfThought, streaming, async, and save/load production semantics are covered by parity or DSEx-native evidence.
DSEx RLM effectiveness is supported by a complete paper-scale reproduction rather than scripted fixture replay.
DSEx provider-free local overhead is benchmarked against DSPy for core paths before any performance claim is made.
DSEx production protocol boundaries for provider training, retrievers, and MCP are exercised through source-checkout protocol gates before being claimed as production surface.

claims.statement: DSEx is installable as a clean Elixir package and its documented public API works outside the source checkout.

claims.scope: Normalized semantic traces; excludes byte-identical Python prompt templates.

blocking_requirements: no live-matched-model matrix or dsex-dspy-parity-campaign artifact found
requirements.threshold: required current_low_cost, frontier_sanity, and historical_research lanes satisfy their policies

claims.scope: Comparative matched-model effectiveness, not the v0.1 provider runtime contract.
claims.statement: DSEx matches Python DSPy on live matched-model benchmark tasks with current prompt contracts, complete instrumentation, runtime-shape evidence, and consistent execution settings.

limitations: v0.1 guarantees deterministic optimizer contracts, not DSPy-equivalent lift.

blocking_requirements: no optimizer-lift-parity artifact found in tmp/optimizer-lift

claims.scope: Comparative optimizer effectiveness for advanced optimizer families.
claims.statement: DSEx optimizer behavior has direct or intentionally-deviating evidence against DSPy for the optimizer surfaces it claims.

limitations: Papillon and HoVer full-scope artifacts are incomplete.

blocking_requirements: no gepa-replication artifact found in tmp/gepa-replication
requirements.threshold: gepa-replication artifact covers AIMEBench, HotpotQABench, hoverBench, IFBench, LiveBenchMathBench, and Papillon with required optimizer, budget, cost, seed, and split-gap fields

claims.statement: DSEx GEPA research claims are supported only by fresh GEPA paper-family replication artifacts that compare baseline, DSPy GEPA, DSEx GEPA, and MIPROv2 with cost, budget, seed, and split-gap metadata; SIMBA may be reported as extra comparator evidence when present.

limitations: Scoped to DSEx-native effectiveness; does not claim paper-scale or matched-internals parity with upstream Optimize Anything.

requirements.threshold: all three non-prompt classes show positive mean lift and a majority of improving runs across at least three live provider-backed seeds

claims.scope: Provider-backed reflective optimization of executable non-prompt text artifacts.
claims.statement: DSEx Optimize Anything improves measurable non-prompt artifacts across multiple seeds using executable held-out evaluators, with provider cost and checkpoint provenance.

limitations: v0.1 claims local contracts and selected live paths, not full upstream parity.

blocking_requirements: no rag-tool-agent-parity artifact found in tmp/rag-tool-agent

claims.scope: Cross-system parity for advanced RAG, tool, and agent workflows.
claims.statement: DSEx RAG, tool, ReAct, agent, CodeAct, ProgramOfThought, streaming, async, and save/load production semantics are covered by parity or DSEx-native evidence.

limitations: The deterministic RLM fixture lane is T0 contract replay and cannot prove effectiveness or long-context parity.

blocking_requirements: no rlm-benchmark-parity artifact found in tmp/rlm-benchmark
requirements.threshold: RLM artifact is T3 paper-scale evidence with a complete paper protocol

claims.scope: Paper-scale RLM long-context effectiveness compared with upstream.
claims.statement: DSEx RLM effectiveness is supported by a complete paper-scale reproduction rather than scripted fixture replay.

limitations: No v0.1 claim that DSEx is faster than DSPy.

blocking_requirements: no overhead-parity artifact found in tmp/overhead
requirements.threshold: all provider-free overhead cases pass within configured ratio

claims.scope: Named-path comparative local overhead; excludes blanket speed claims.
claims.statement: DSEx provider-free local overhead is benchmarked against DSPy for core paths before any performance claim is made.

blocking_requirements: no protocol_gates source-checkout gate evidence artifact found in tmp/gate-evidence; run mix dsex.gate_evidence --gate protocol_gates --mix-task protocol.check

claims.scope: Provider-compatible local protocol boundaries; excludes paid training completion.
claims.statement: DSEx production protocol boundaries for provider training, retrievers, and MCP are exercised through source-checkout protocol gates before being claimed as production surface.

requirements.threshold: verified current-schema artifact independently recomputes all deterministic cases and zero runtime leaks

claims.scope: Provider-free repeated failure and recovery behavior with verified runtime leak accounting.
claims.statement: DSEx deterministic cancellation, timeout, bounded concurrency, partial-stream failure, retry/idempotency, and optimizer resume recovery paths pass the canonical T0 campaign without runtime leaks.

limitations: The current deterministic campaign is T0 evidence and cannot establish live provider, training, retrieval, tool, or agent recovery.

requirements.threshold: verified deterministic T0 authority plus valid completed live rows for both required recovery campaigns

claims.scope: Completed live provider and integration recovery, beyond deterministic protocol simulation.
claims.statement: DSEx failure recovery has verified completed live evidence for provider retry/timeout/idempotency and integrated training, retrieval, tool, and agent recovery.

claims.limitation: One or more release-blocking public claims lack fresh passing evidence.
